questions.q: What does { FIXED [Customer Name] : SUM([Sales]) } compute?
options: Total sales per customer, the same value regardless of what else is on the view
Total sales per order, changing as you add dimensions to the view
The average sales across all customers combined into one number
A running total of sales sorted by customer name
questions.explain: FIXED computes at exactly the dimension(s) listed — here, Customer Name — independent of the view's own grain, so it stays stable no matter what else is on Rows or Columns.

questions.q: What does { FIXED : AVG([Sales]) } — an empty FIXED scope — return?
options: One number: the overall average sale amount across the entire table, repeated on every row
An error, because FIXED requires at least one dimension
The average sales per customer
The average of only the visible rows after filtering
questions.explain: An empty FIXED scope means the whole table — it's the LOD equivalent of a grand total that doesn't change as the view is sliced.

questions.q: A regular (non-context) dimension filter on Region is applied to the view. Does a { FIXED [Customer Name] : SUM([Sales]) } calculation reflect that filter?
options: No — regular dimension filters run after FIXED calculates, so FIXED still sees the unfiltered data
Yes — all filters always apply before any calculation
Yes, but only for numeric measures
No, because FIXED expressions ignore all filters permanently, with no way to change that
questions.explain: Regular dimension filters apply after FIXED has already computed. To make a filter apply before FIXED, you have to explicitly promote it to a context filter.

questions.q: How do you make a regular filter apply before a FIXED LOD calculation runs?
options: Right-click the filter pill and select Add to Context
Rewrite the FIXED expression using INCLUDE instead
Move the filter from Rows to Columns
There is no way to do this — FIXED always ignores every filter
questions.explain: Promoting a filter to a context filter makes it run before FIXED (and other LOD) calculations, unlike an ordinary dimension filter.

questions.q: What does { FIXED [Customer Name] : MIN([Order Date]) } give you, and why is it useful?
options: Each customer's first purchase date, stable across any view — useful for cohort or new-vs-returning analysis
The most recent order date across all customers
A count of how many orders each customer has placed
The date the calculation was created in the workbook
questions.explain: FIXED locks MIN([Order Date]) to the Customer Name grain, giving each customer's earliest order date — a common building block for cohort-style analysis, expanded on in Lesson 73.
